title: Register and secure a robot proximity switch beneath its actuator
objective: Using an independently authored full-scale fixture grounded in the AZ-100 procedure, retract the rigid cylinder, partially loosen the switch-mount screws, slide the proximity switch beneath its actuator until it registers, tighten it without losing registration, and repeat at the extended endpoint.
success_conditions: At both retracted and extended endpoints, robot-applied motions alone place the actuator past the switch centerline, maintain a sensing gap of at most 6 mm, trigger the indicator solely through physical relative pose, and leave the switch secured for 3 seconds after release. Zero score for powered adjustment, skipping initial retraction, moving the actuator mount as a shortcut, registering only one endpoint, actuator collision, loose or stripped screws, dropped tools, scripted sensor success, teleportation, or state overwrite. Partial credit is awarded for safe initialization, correct screw release, one geometrically valid endpoint, and registration retained after tightening.
industrial_value: The AZ-100 maintenance manual requires proximity-switch adjustment after position changes and specifies registration at both cylinder endpoints. The task therefore represents recurring calibration of an industrial robot’s motion-limit sensing rather than generic switch operation.
dexterity: Moderate-to-high: it combines partial fastener release, constrained sliding, feedback-guided registration, sub-centimeter clearance control, holding against tightening reaction, and repetition across two articulated states.

evidence.locator: AZ-100 Series Robot Installation and Maintenance Manual, page 30, section 4.2.1, step 3
AZ-100 Series Robot Installation and Maintenance Manual, page 30, section 4.2.1, note

asset_plan: Build a clearly labeled representative, not exact-product, rigid fixture with a slotted switch bracket, retained mount screws, rigid actuator, and two cylinder endpoints matching the documented arrangement. Use the documented 6 mm boundary and over-center requirement. Choose and record testable modeling assumptions for screw size, slot length, tightening window, cylinder stroke, and sensor hysteresis; calibrate them on the fixture before scoring. Implement the indicator only as a function of actuator-to-sensor geometry. First validate screw retention, sliding only while loosened, the 6 mm boundary, over-center registration, collision rejection, tightening drift, reset repeatability, fingertip clearance, and YAM reach in Isaac Sim 6.1.0 at YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730.
risk: The fixture will not claim to reproduce exact proprietary AZ-100 dimensions. Remaining unspecified dimensions are nonessential, explicitly testable fixture parameters; the sourced retention mechanism—screws clamping a sliding switch mount—and sensing relationship are sufficient. A synchronized novelty review must still be repeated before submission because cached records are not authoritative live state.
